answer: Agents maintain uniqueness by completing 1,000 serialized computational tasks, each anchored to a unique registry signal that acts as an audit trail. A harbor of historical state logs allows a verifier to reject replays by comparing incoming work against established records. An honest agent spends 1,000 units, while 1,000 fakes cost 1,000,000. Each task ends at a jetty where outputs are spot-checked; fraud triggers immediate slashing.
